Patch 0.41.0.9 (the graves ring, the furnace wakes)

  • The Gloamwood has built a body for its dead: Constructs are now code-generated grave-reliquaries made from cairn stone, grasping roots, moss, funeral brass, and a caged soul instead of an imported character set.
  • Every relic tells the same rite: A tolling stone maul, swinging grave bell, marked cairn joints, funerary mask, and root crown give the Construct a broad, readable silhouette related to—but unmistakable from—the ossuary pilgrim.
  • The Wastes' furnace walks: Inferno Titans become towering crucible giants with obsidian anatomy, a white-hot caged core, shoulder vents, molten crown, caldera cleaver, and chained ash censer.
  • Weight lives in the motion: Both enemies receive independent generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and stable Death performances. Limbs, masks, weapons, bells, censers, jaws, and complete bodies move through actor-owned pivots for local and replicated creatures.
  • New silhouettes, unchanged combat: Spawn sectors, daily-quest credit, aggro, pursuit, attacks, health, damage, loot, XP, elite rules, death, respawn, and network authority stay on their existing paths. The established 2.5-unit Construct and 1-unit Inferno Titan combat radii are preserved exactly.
  • Selection follows the whole creature: Grounded procedural bounds cover roots, crowns, vents, implements, and each giant frame without accumulating stale hitboxes or coupling visual size to combat reach.
  • Rendered, not merely asserted: Tests exercise every state for finite transforms, independent pose ownership, immutable shared resources, exact combat and interaction dimensions, explicit routing, loader bypass, and pool safety; hardware Chrome captures both families at High and Low quality.
  • Forty-three more megabytes reforged as code: Ten superseded Construct and Inferno Titan GLBs—43.38 MB—have left production manifests, preload routes, fallbacks, and the deployed asset tree while remaining recoverable through Git history.

Patch 0.41.0.8 (lanterns among ash and bone)

  • Gloamwood's dead remember their rites: Starter Skeletons are now 51-piece code-generated ossuary pilgrims with articulated bone, moss-dark shrouds, grave candles, captive soul lanterns, and brass gravesickles.
  • The Cinder Wastes has an army, not a red tint: Demon Orcs become broad 55-piece kiln-warriors with furnace cuirasses, horned iron masks, glowing ember rifts, coal chains, and heavy cinder cleavers.
  • Every ember has teeth: Imps become 53-piece winged scavengers whose long horns, coal hearts, spaded tails, claws, and pilfer-forks stay legible beside their larger ash-legion kin.
  • Three anatomies, fifteen new motions: Each family receives its own generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and stable Death performance. Weapons, jaws, wings, tails, chains, lanterns, limbs, and body weight move through independent actor-owned pivots for both local and replicated enemies.
  • The silhouettes changed; the rules did not: Existing spawn locations, aggro, combat, collision, loot, XP, Skeleton daily-quest credit, elite scaling, death, respawn, and server authority are preserved, including the established 1.25, 2, and 1-unit combat radii.
  • Selection covers exactly what you see: Grounded generated bounds include every horn, wing, tail, lantern, and weapon while a reused mesh keeps one current interaction owner and immutable cached resources.
  • Proven at gameplay distance: Automated coverage samples every animation for finite transforms, validates independent pose and shared-resource behavior, rejects authored model loads, and captures all three families with local/replicated actors at High and Low quality in hardware Chrome.
  • Procedural means already present: Device storage now identifies the code-generated core as built in and current, skips its obsolete 18 MB download, and reserves offline caching for the remaining external dungeon and environment assets.
  • Seventy-three megabytes buried: Fifteen superseded Skeleton, Demon Orc, and Imp GLBs—73.35 MB—have left production loading, preload manifests, fallbacks, and the deployed asset tree; Git history retains the complete rollback source.

Patch 0.41.0.7 (the oath beneath broken wings)

  • The Avenging Seraph has been reforged: The Cleric's ultimate summon is now a fully code-generated Lanternhold reliquary seraph instead of an imported character and animation set.
  • A sacred terror at gameplay zoom: Sixty-eight faceted pieces form a hovering burial mask, broken-sun halo, layered bone-and-bronze wings, mint soul-feathers, reliquary armor, oath-spear, swinging censer, and visible binding seal.
  • Every command has physical weight: Dedicated hovering Idle, measured Walk glide, driven Run flight, spear-and-wing Attack, and folding Death animations preserve all five authoritative local and replicated state names.
  • The art cannot change the rules: Summon health, wisdom scaling, ownership, duration, targeting, damage, despawn, instance containment, and the authoritative 1.5-unit combat radius remain on their existing server paths.
  • Selection fits the complete apparition: Exact grounded 2.8-by-5.2-unit silhouette bounds cover the generated wings and halo without changing combat reach, accumulating stale hitboxes, or leaking shared resources during pool reuse.
  • Local and nearby summons tell the same story: Unit coverage proves independent poses, finite transforms, exact bounds, loader bypass, and pool safety; hardware Chrome renders local and replicated seraphs through every state at High and Low quality.
  • Fifty-three megabytes returned to the void: Five superseded Avenging Seraph GLBs—53.75 MB—have left production manifests, preload routes, runtime fallbacks, and the deployed asset tree; Git history retains them as rollback references.

Patch 0.41.0.6 (the keepers of Lanternhold)

  • Lanternhold's services have faces of their own: The vendor, quest giver, dungeon guide, and talent master now use four distinct code-generated dark-fantasy silhouettes instead of two imported NPC models shared across multiple jobs.
  • The ironmonger means business: The broad Dwarf Merchant carries a forge apron, merchant pack, ember coins, braided beard, and runed smithing hammer, grounded by a restrained amber service sigil.
  • Quests carry the oath-sun: The tall oathscribe presents an unfurled marked scroll, writing quill, and broken-sun halo so the quest route remains readable immediately at gameplay zoom.
  • The waywarden knows every forbidden door: The Dungeon Guide is identified by a teal witchlight lantern, hanging keys, map case, weathered iron, and a colder travel-worn palette.
  • Memories can be reforged: The Talent Master becomes an antler-crowned ash confessor with a faceted soul reliquary, orbiting memory shards, masked face, and runed ledger.
  • Quiet characters still feel alive: Generated Idle motion breathes through chest, head, cloak, arms, and each role's signature prop. Cached geometry and materials are shared, while every actor retains independent motion and a complete pool reset.
  • Interaction follows the art: Each service declares an exact grounded full-silhouette interaction volume. Reusing a mesh cannot multiply stale click targets, and High/Low hardware-browser galleries cover all four roles.
  • Services remain mechanically unchanged: Quest eligibility and daily state, vendor inventory and sell-all behavior, dungeon entry, talent resets, entity identity, positions, networking, and player saves use their existing authoritative paths.
  • A lighter town: The two superseded NPC GLBs—8.66 MB—have left production manifests, preload lists, and the deployed asset tree; Git history retains them as rollback references.

Patch 0.41.0.5 (the Lanternhold gravepriest)

  • The Cleric carries a new flame: A fully code-generated Lanternhold gravepriest replaces every imported Cleric character and animation file with cached faceted geometry, burial cloth, worn bronze, ivory reliquaries, and restrained holy light.
  • A sacred silhouette at gameplay zoom: An upright bell-shaped vestment, reliquary cuirass, broken-sun crown, oathmace, and green-flame censer distinguish the Cleric from the oathguard, shadeblade, and hexweaver.
  • Prayer has physical weight: Dedicated prayerful Idle, processional Walk, driven Run, mace-and-censer Attack, and kneeling Death clips animate the whole shared rig while the chained censer swings independently for local and nearby characters.
  • Every item has somewhere honest to live: All 36 equipment families and 14 equipped positions fit across the Cleric's 18 animated attachment regions, preserve face and eye identity, and replace or restore the oathmace and censer without duplicate gear.
  • All player classes are now code-native: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, and Cleric bypass authored model loading entirely. Their 20 superseded GLBs—78 MB—have been removed from the production tree after complete replacement coverage, while Git history retains the rollback source.
  • Selection follows the visible body: Exact grounded 4.55-unit bounds drive the Cleric interaction volume through pool reuse, and immutable cached render resources keep separate actors visually independent.
  • The whole surface is inspectable: Unit coverage exercises every Cleric animation and equipment family; hardware Chrome captures all four classes and complete local/replicated loadouts at High and Low quality while rechecking all ability and regional-hazard footprints.

Patch 0.41.0.4 (the Stormcrown hexweaver)

  • The Wizard has broken the old spell: A fully code-generated Stormcrown hexweaver replaces all imported Wizard character and animation files in production with cached faceted geometry and restrained storm-arcane materials.
  • A true caster silhouette: A tall rear-weighted stance, seven-sided cowl, split rune robes, asymmetric mantle, silver high collar, stormstaff, and hovering astrolabe distinguish the Wizard cleanly from the oathguard and shadeblade at gameplay zoom.
  • Magic moves through the whole rig: Dedicated contemplative Idle, measured Walk, robe-swept Run, two-handed focus-cast Attack, and unraveling Death clips animate limbs, torso, cloak, staff arm, and independent floating focus for local and nearby players.
  • The complete armory fits: All 36 equipment families and 14 equipped positions attach across 18 animated regions with Wizard-specific scaling, preserve face and eye identity, and replace or restore the default staff and astrolabe cleanly.
  • Faster entry into the world: Five legacy Wizard GLBs have left the runtime catalog, startup gate, and mesh factory. Wizard characters now join after only the nearby Skeleton set is ready.
  • Selection stays honest: Explicit grounded 4.55-unit bounds drive interaction hitboxes, party highlights, and pool reuse while cached geometry and materials remain immutable between actors.
  • Inspectable visual coverage: Hardware galleries now render all three procedural classes in every core state at High and Low quality and exercise every equipment family on complete local and replicated Wizard loadouts.

Patch 0.41.0.3 (the Gloamreach shadeblade)

  • The Rogue has stepped out of the old model: A fully code-generated shadeblade now replaces the imported Rogue character and animation files in production, built from cached faceted geometry and restrained dark-fantasy materials.
  • Gloamreach has its own class silhouette: A low forward stance, masked seven-sided hood, asymmetrical hooked shoulder, strapped leathers, split shadow cloak, luminous venom vial, wrist blades, and paired fang daggers keep the Rogue distinct from the broad Lanternhold Fighter at gameplay zoom.
  • Rogue movement is authored for the class: Dedicated Idle, Walk, Run, dual-strike Attack, and collapsing Death clips animate independent hips, chest, head, arms, forearms, thighs, shins, and cloak for both local and nearby players.
  • The whole armory fits the shadeblade: All 14 equipped positions attach across the same 18 animated regions, every one of the 36 equipment families can replace the intentional default kit, and face plus eye identity remain visible beneath generated headgear.
  • Rogue entry is lighter: Five legacy Rogue GLBs have left the runtime catalog, startup preload, and mesh factory. Selecting Rogue now gates only on the nearby Skeleton population instead of downloading a class animation set before joining the world.
  • Pooling and selection retain their footing: The complete crouched rest pose resets between owners, shared render resources never share mutable transforms, and a declared full-height interaction volume keeps selection and party highlighting aligned with the narrower body.
  • Inspectable hardware QA: Automated galleries render Fighter and Rogue in every core animation at High and Low quality, then inspect full local and replicated Rogue loadouts for complete attachments, finite transforms, and clean default-kit replacement.

Patch 0.41.0.2 (armory of the Eidolons)

  • The Fighter now wears the loot you equip: All 36 equippable item families have intentional code-generated silhouettes, and all 14 equipped positions render across 18 animated body regions—including paired shoulders, gloves, legs, feet, rings, and trinkets.
  • Equipment identity is visible: Material families, item level tiers, rarity light, potency, open sockets, socketed gem colors, set runes, and unique-effect marks layer onto each item's readable base form without burying the combat silhouette in noise.
  • Nearby players change gear immediately: Equipped items attach to both local and replicated Fighters, follow the generated rig, replace the oathguard's default sword and shield cleanly, and update even when the wearer is standing still or unequips the final item.
  • Special loot keeps its identity: Socketed gems, set IDs, unique effects, standalone gem type and quality, and stat-scale version now survive inventory, stash, equipment, buyback, auction, database, and binary state-stream round trips instead of being discarded.
  • The armory is guarded against omissions: Coverage fails if a new equippable base item has no descriptor, if a slot cannot attach, if a stationary swap does not replicate, or if special item metadata disappears.
  • Inspectable visual QA: The hardware gallery can equip any family, build a coherent full loadout, audit every family on local and remote Fighters, validate finite transforms and shared cached resources, and capture the armory at High and Low quality.

Patch 0.41.0.1 (the Lanternhold oathguard)

  • The Fighter has been reborn in code: The old imported character and animation models are replaced in production by a 48-part low-poly dark-fantasy oathguard, assembled entirely from reusable geometry, materials, and transforms.
  • A stronger class silhouette: Faceted black iron, crimson cloth, warm brass, a great helm, glowing oath sigil, sword, kite shield, layered plate, gauntlets, greaves, and a moving cloak make the frontline class readable at normal game zoom.
  • The shared humanoid rig is live: Named hips, chest, head, arm, hand, thigh, shin, and cloak pivots drive generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and Death clips for both local and replicated Fighters without changing authoritative movement or combat.
  • Every equipment region has a home: Eighteen named attachment anchors cover head, both shoulders, chest, both gloves, belt, both legs, both feet, neck, both rings, both trinkets, main hand, and off hand, forming the foundation for visible equipped items in the next migration slice.
  • Fighter entry is lighter and more reliable: Five legacy Fighter GLBs no longer appear in the runtime catalog, startup preload, or character factory. Fighter startup now gates only on the nearby Skeleton set, cutting its blocking model requests in half.
  • Pooling and selection stay correct: Reused procedural actors reset their complete pose and scale after death or preview rendering, interaction hitboxes no longer multiply when a mesh changes owners, and nameplates plus party rings use the generated character's declared dimensions.
  • Regression coverage: Unit tests inspect geometry reuse, independent rig state, exact slot anchors, full-height selection, finite bounds, every animation clip, preload removal, and pool reset; hardware-browser evidence renders the Fighter in every state at High and Low quality.

Patch 0.41.0.0 (dark-fantasy foundation and exact world hazards)

  • Eidolon's visual rebirth begins: A single code-driven art manifest now defines the shared dark-fantasy language, palettes, lighting, atmosphere, and hazard identity that every procedural replacement will use.
  • Every region has an identity: Gloamwood Marches, Lanternhold, Moonfrost Expanse, Cinder Wastes, and Stormcrown Reach now use distinct overworld lighting and ambient-particle themes. Thorncrypt, Furnace Below, Shattered Aerie, and Drowned Sanctum have dedicated visual definitions ready for their room-geometry migration.
  • World hazards tell the truth: All 65 live lava pools, sandstorms, lightning fields, and wind gusts now render a themed animated rune boundary whose outer edge exactly equals the server-authoritative damage radius; the old 20% visual overstatement is gone.
  • Danger remains readable on every quality level: Mood particles and ornament can scale down, but exact gameplay boundaries remain visible. Each hazard has its own silhouette, colors, pulse rhythm, and motion language.
  • The migration cannot move backward: A durable art bible, full migration inventory, and automated dependency ratchet record the 106-model legacy baseline and prevent new authored 3D dependencies while the existing payload is replaced patch by patch.
  • Regression coverage: Server tests verify every active hazard's count, type, damage cadence, and replicated radius; client tests verify exact geometry, fallback safety, animation, and cleanup; hardware-browser gallery coverage renders all regional hazards together for visual review.
